name: Strawberry
intro: A strawberry is a sweet red fruit. It grows on a leafy green plant.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A ripe strawberry is bright red.
It is juicy and sweet.
Tiny seeds cover the outside of the fruit.
One strawberry has about 200 seeds!
The plant has green leaves and small flowers.

sections.title: Where does it grow?
sentences: Strawberries grow well in most parts of the world.
They grow on big farms and in home gardens.
Some people grow them in pots.
The first garden strawberry came from France.

sections.title: What does it need?
sentences: A strawberry plant needs lots of sun.
It needs soil that drains water well.
It needs water often because its roots are short.
It needs space so air can move around it.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A strawberry plant grows flowers first.
Bees carry pollen to the flowers.
Then the flowers turn into fruit.
The plant sends out long stems called runners.
Runners grow roots and make new plants.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A strawberry is not a true berry.
Strawberries do not get riper after they are picked.
Strawberries have lots of vitamin C.
Some Native American groups call the June full moon the Strawberry Moon.
Birds, deer, and squirrels eat wild strawberries.

vocab.meaning: A long stem that grows along the ground and makes a new plant.
Yellow dust that flowers need to make fruit.
A small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
